Abstract:

This Report presents the design and implementation of a digital twin framework for a low-cost collaborative robot using the Robot Operating System (ROS 2) and Gazebo. The proposed framework establishes bidirectional communication between the physical robot and its virtual model, allowing real-time simulation, monitoring, and synchronization of robot states. The robot is modeled using unified robot description format &nbspand integrated into the Gazebo simulation environment to accurately replicate its kinematic and dynamic behavior. Joint states, control commands, and sensor information are continuously exchanged through ROS middleware, enabling synchronized operation between the physical and virtual environments. The physical igus ReBeL robot is integrated with a virtual robot model developed using unified robot description format. ROS 2 serves as the communication and integration middleware, while Gazebo provides the simulation environment and RViz2 provides robot-state visualization.

The proposed architecture provides an effective, scalable, and cost-efficient digital twin solution suitable for research laboratories and small- and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises.The bidirectional communication ensures synchronization between the virtual and physical systems.

The framework also serves as a foundation for future applications including predictive maintenance, AI-assisted control, and intelligent manufacturing.
